Hi Sarah —

Great to meet on today’s call. Thanks for walking us through MedHealth’s use case (patient intake forms + clinical notes processing for triage). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap
- You plan to send PHI (patient identifiers, clinical notes) to an inference endpoint for classification/enrichment.
- Primary concerns: BAA availability, retention/ERASURE controls, encryption, and vendor questionnaire.

Redwood summary (short):
- BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA for eligible deployments (Dedicated and Private).
- Deployment eligibility: Hosted (public shared API) is NOT eligible for PHI. Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPU pools) and Private (VPC / on-prem) are eligible and standard path for PHI.
- Security posture: SOC 2 Type II, encryption in transit and at rest, KMS/HSM options for Private and Dedicated, configurable token/retention policies, and ability to disable KV/prefix caching for PHI pipelines.

Requests / next steps
1) Please send the vendor security questionnaire when convenient (or upload to the secure drive link below).
2) We’ll start a security review and have our security engineer (cc’d) triage the questionnaire.
3) I’ll share our BAA template and a short deployment guidance doc (attached). If things look good we can route the BAA to DocuSign.
4) If possible, confirm expected monthly volume (requests/day) and whether you expect long-lived context (large documents) vs short single-field inference. This helps sizing for Dedicated.

Attachments: Redwood_BAA_template.pdf (draft), HIPAA_Deployment_Guide.pdf
Secure upload: https://drive.google.com/secure/medhealth-questionnaire-upload

I’ll let Dylan and our security lead take the questionnaire once you send it — happy to set a security deep-dive next week if helpful.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Marissa

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the questionnaire — I see the upload and the local copy attached. Answers inline to your high-level questions below; Neha (cc) will follow up with more detail and start working through the questionnaire.

1) Hosted API and PHI
- Hosted/shared API is not an approved path for PHI. The isolation and contractual controls we require for BAA-covered PHI are only available on Dedicated or Private deployments. BYOK on Hosted does not change the shared control plane and is therefore not sufficient for PHI compliance.

2) Log and audit access
- Access to request/response payloads is restricted by role. For Dedicated and Private we can limit access to a small set of platform operators and provide an audit trail. We log access events and can provide audit extracts on request as part of the security/BAA process. Persistent storage of payloads is configurable; for PHI we recommend retention=0 and disable KV/prefix caching.

3) BAA template
- The BAA I attached is our standard draft and is typically redlineable. Legal reviews are expected; we can route a DocuSign link once your team indicates readiness.

Additional specifics
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II; we can provide the attestation during security review.
- Encryption: TLS in transit + AES-256 at rest; Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys (KMS / HSM).
- KV cache: For PHI workflows we disable prefix/KV caching and avoid persistent intermediate storage.

Proposed next steps
1) Neha will triage your questionnaire and ask any follow-ups (target: 2 business days).
2) If there are no showstoppers, we’ll propose a Dedicated sizing and draft BAA redline window and schedule a 30–45 min security call.
3) If you prefer Private (VPC or on-prem), we can provide a deployment checklist and quote — that timeline is longer (infra lead time).

DocuSign BAA draft (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/baa-draft-RDW-2467
Secure upload: https://drive.google.com/secure/medhealth-questionnaire-upload

Neha / Dylan — assigning to you both to start questionnaire review. Sarah — please call out any specific needed SLAs or retention rules in the questionnaire fields.

Thanks,
Marissa
